traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Menispermaceae: leaves alternate; leaves usually simple, rarely compound; veins pinnate or palmate; stipules absent; plants usually dioecious, sometimes monoecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems usually woody, rarely herbaceous; flowers in panicles or in cymes, rarely solitary; flowers usually actinomorphic, rarely zygomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, rarely tepals; fruit usually aggregate, sometimes nut; parts of each whorl 3; stamens (1-) 6 (-40); carpels (1-) 3 to 30. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
